verdict.tagline: Terrifying atmosphere and iconic sound design hampered by severe technical hiccups.
for_you_if: you want a deeply atmospheric psychological horror experience
you enjoy complex puzzles and dense environmental storytelling
you appreciate haunting soundtracks and oppressive tension

you want fast-paced and varied combat mechanics
you encounter game crashes and stuttering
you dislike padded sections in extended campaigns

citations.review_text:
Never been so quick to leave a bad review for a game, or even any review as a matter of fact. But I hated this game. I hated the 1 dimensional combat. I hated that there is no optimization and even with a great setup -which lets me play Resident Evil Requiem (a game with far bigger areas and a lot better visuals) smoothly with stable and high FPS- I got constant stutters and FPS drops for very small visual cues. Which is ironic since your eyesight range is literally 5 meters max. I hated the fact that the game doesn't give any explanations to puzzles and just mark the locations on your map, so you find yourself following the map without knowing why are you going where you are going and how the hell you got the location marked on your map. I hate the way you discover the area, every door looks the same so you want to go check inside but its not interactable and your only cue is the white dot that appears when you get close to an interactable object. Even when you find a loot (which is almost as rare as triple rainbows) it turns out to be a freaking health recovery item 90% of the time. Also, the game uses "White cloth" like how Resident Evil uses "Yellow Paint", but just in a terrible way that it can't really guide you properly even with the infamous "Yellow Paint" method. I won't really get into the story as I haven't played the game long enough, but for the amount of time I played this game, I got sick of only hearing "My Wife" and "Our special place" with no context at all. The game failed to give me any motivation to make me play it with all these technical issues and vague and empty puzzles in a vague and empty town. I would say play this only if you played the original in your childhood and want to feel nostalgic. If its your first entry of the series, don't bother. I can guarantee you will not enjoy the first 70 minutes of the game one bit. Cant speak for the rest of it.

Edit: requested refund. This series lost me forever as a player with this game. I doubt I…

Im still on a 3060 and guess what, i still could play most games very good at 1080p. Even games like Space Marine2 run with 60 FPS for me. But this one already starts with low FPS in the starting area where nothing happens. No matter what setting i use. That is extremly dissappointing and the first game since a very long time for me which has such extreme performance issues. Considering how many people praise Bloober Team for this and many other games i really cant believe it actually. But yeah some times you have bad luck i guess :-/

(For 70 bucks you should able expect some optimization i think...)

DO NOT BUY IT UNTIL IT GIVES BETTER PERFORMANCE!

TERRIBLE OPTIMIZATION. EVEN WITH RX9070XT, I CANT GET STABLE 60 FPS ON 4k WITH RT. WHEN I TRY TO USE OPTISCALER FOR FSR4 THE GAME CRASHES ALL THE TIME! I MEAN WTF? WHAT IS IT TO DO WITH OPTISCALER? 

YOU GUYS HAVE TO BE SHAMEFUL FOR REALEASING THIS UNOPTIMIZED GAME.

This is an another stupid remake which doesn't even run lemme explain 

First I bought the game well and good I got the money everything was fine then installed it pretty quick so happy to play it cuz I have heard that it is one of the most spooky game of all time so after installing I played it for exactly 1hr after that BINGO the game CRASHED so i relaunched it didn't work i tried to restart my PC didn't work i then watched some youtube and added dx11 in the launch options  didn't work it was an absolute waste trying to do every possible things to run this BS so I finally quit trying and raise a refund request.

So don't waste your time people just don't buy this crap save some time go to burger king and enjoy.

citations.review_text:
The source material is a masterpiece, the game is gorgeous, I would probably give it an 8.5-9/10.. but this is a strong do not recommend for UE5 and crashing. 

Half the time on startup it crashes and then 100% of the time if I go to re load a save it crashes. Settings don't matter it's garbage optimization and programming. Bloober did this with Cronos too, every time I needed to load a game I held my breath for a crash. 

I have a common middle upper tier rig. Unacceptable.
I'm sure it has great story and all, but optimization is just awful in some parts of the game I'm getting 40-50 fps at 1080p lowest settings using dlss quality with this rig.

Konami making the scariest idea for a game ever: American Mid-Western Small Mining Town Aesthetics, with Southern European Poverty and Side Characters With Eastern European Personalities.

Silent Hill 2 remake is a, well... a good remake of a great game that everyone pretends to have played.

But of course, even with a rig optimized for Unreal engine, frame issues are aplenty and the performance is rather inconsistent early in the game. Thankfully, a few hours past the beginning, it was rather smooth on high settings and resolution. As always, Unreal needed some time to cache most of the assets and any jitters I got after that was simply new environments loading in at once. 

Honestly, I hoped for better performance after how excellent MGS3 remake ended up running and looking... and playing, helped tremendously by the fact it was a 1:1 remake and utilized loading screens. Personally, I would prefer Unreal games have the option for loading screens than to deal with large loss of frames and performance for several seconds at a time, there were two occasions where I had about a dozen seconds of suboptimal frames in new areas. 

Ultimately, Silent Hill 2 is one of the most legendary games ever made and it has a presence in the public consciousness of culture in a way that it truly sells the fact that video games are perhaps the greatest form of art. Silent Hill 2, remake and original, has one of the most iconic presentations of any piece of media ever and with some of the most great designs for any levels, enemies, bosses and characters. Iconic does not begin to scratch a single centimeter of rust off the surface of the game's absolute and all embodied legacy that exists to this day.

All of this being said and objectively true, I must now offer an insanely unpopular opinion. I think Silent Hill 2 is a conceptually and artistically high brow work of art, but its not my favourite Silent Hill and I don't think it ever had a chance of being. The first Silent Hill…

As much as I like the visuals, atmosphere and new fighting gameplay, I still prefer the OG Silent HIll 2.
This remake is flawed by the issue most UE5 slop games have: utterly ♥♥♥♥ performance up to the degree it's unbareable and almost impossible to gain stable 60fps even with upscaling turned on. Even worse, changing the settings has barely any effect on the fps what so ever.

thumbs down because the community is very toxic and will spoil basically everything then double down on being jerks. no i do not recommend this game. It also stutters all the time and has terrible optimizations.

Game itself is great, atmosphere, story, enemies but I cannot recommend it due to optimization, stutters everywhere. It doesnt matter if I put it on low or high settings, same ♥♥♥♥. I know my pc is a little bit older but I can still run most of the new games without any hiccups, hopefully unreal is not answer for everything

I just didn't like it. Game controls feels so slow and i think this game has a huge optimization issues as i realised. While i have 7800 XT i can not get even 60fps. The story must bee good, but with this bad controls i can not recommend.

Silent Hill 2 is straight up insane.

The story is easily the best narrative I’ve ever experienced in a horror game. The plot twists are absolutely wild and even the side characters like Eddie, Laura, Angela and Maria all have so much depth and tragic backstories. Angela’s story especially hit me really hard. The atmosphere in this game is by far the best horror atmosphere I’ve ever felt. It’s pure dread and sadness mixed together in the most beautiful way.
The amount of insane details everywhere is crazy. Every corner, every sound, every little thing feels so carefully made. The graphics look beautiful and the locations are incredibly atmospheric.
The puzzles are cool and varied, and the combat is actually pretty fun too.

Of course it’s not perfect. The performance can be rough sometimes. I had a few crashes and random FPS drops. There’s also way too much enemy spam. I liked the combat, but I would’ve preferred fewer but stronger enemies instead of getting swarmed all the time. Some sections also felt a bit too long and stretched out.
Still, even with those problems, this game is absolutely crazy good. On Standard it was a bit too easy for me, but overall it’s one of the strongest experiences I’ve had in years. If you like psychological horror, this is a must-play. Highly recommended.

9/10

its a good remake sure, better than most remakes and remasters being released today, but its just too stretched out to the point its not even fun sometimes, just doing too much to make the game longer, original was 4-5 hours long while this is 11-12 hours long, combat can get repetitive so fast and the modern gameplay sure is more accessible but just makes the game way less unique and basic, feels like resident evil 2 remake, voice acting is also more basic and sounds like a netflix dub, its still a good game nonetheless, good for people who just cant stand tank controls because they're too hard and confusing!!!!! Game so unoptimized that James looks like a traumatized Version of PewDiePie whenever you try to save the Game..


I am disappointed actually how badly optimized the game is... RE:Requiem is far better optimized.. :/ my specs should be able to run the game man..

claims.claim: Reviewers state that certain areas and sections of the game feel padded out, stretched, or too long.

citations.review_text:
This game has a great atmosphere and graphics are nice. It maintains its creepy atmosphere throughout the whole game, and the enemy designs are very well done. The story is also really good.

However, I find that the game drags on in some areas, like the hospital, which breaks immersion and leads to more frustrating moments rather than scary ones. The gameplay loop barely changes which can get tedious quickly. While the enemies are really interesting initially, they get old quick, besides some of the boss encounters. While you do eventually get a few weapon types, the combat remains the same; shoot an enemy to get them down and finish them with the melee weapon, so it gets old quickly. 

I am not even finished with the game but there are still 2 more areas for me to complete and it 's getting increasingly more tedious pushing through all the areas. 

The original defintely has better pacing and the time it takes to complete each area is a lot more reasonable. I will probably be taking a break from the game before I return to finish it because playing the game really does burn me out.

Not the Silent Hill 2 I know and love. Pyramid Head's intro scenes are changed to be less graphic, the music is overdone and orchestral, they removed the "James talking to doctors" cutscene you can get in the Hotel, no "Born from a Wish", too many enemies, too long and padded out, enemies are less intimidating and lost their personality, Maria's clothing is censored and the game mocks her original outfit, the Abstract Daddy bossfight is censored and less effective, Mary is cracking jokes in one of her final scenes where James confesses. They also removed the Great Knife weapon. Maria's prison cell cutscene looks like a joke, no shadows under her eyes, etc. All in all, a soulless remake and I regret playing more than 2 hours so I cannot refund.

I have played numerous horror games over the years from outlast, resident evil, fnaf etc. I REALLY wanted to like this game i really did. BUT I think it is better as  love letter to the original fans who played it years ago as opposed to new people. The story is extremely slow, I understand that this is a mostly heavily symbolic game but that is just one of the issues. The enemies are very repetitive there is a monster with legs whose man goal is to run from you when you see it and just hide behind corners waiting to ambush you. The dread and atmosphere which they do a very good job at building is often wasted. The puzzles which were interesting and fun at first just became tedious and consistently slowed down the gameplay even more after the halfway point. Not to mention the constant back tracking through areas. So much so there is literally a section of the game where you spend hours in an area then get thrown into a type of "Upside down"(strangers thing reference) version of the exact same place you spent hours navigating. I was fortunate enough to not experience too many stuttering issues if I played at 1440p and locked the fps at 60. Though if you run through halls too fast the frames will drop. I respect this franchise as a classic and their fans. I also understand this game probably has some amazing lore that is better consumed in a video essay on YouTube than to play it. But after being ambushed by the same enemy(leg monster) hiding behind a wall for the 3rd time in 2 minutes EVEN WITH ME having maybe only 5 hours left in the game I just couldn't take it anymore and uninstalled it. 

My computer specs. Ryzen 7 3800x ,16Gb of DDR4, 5070ti

Overall, it's a good remake. I think it could have been a much more enjoyable experience if it lasted around 8 hours.

Cons:
- Having to clear buildings twice... clearing the original is OK, but the rusty versions are boring.
- The monsters respawning is BS.
- The open map is unnecessary. There's nothing important on the map, no reason is given to try to enter buildings, you can easily skip them, so why an open map? Also, not knowing where to go is frustrating. You're constantly running around in the streets with creatures everywhere.
- Good graphics but bad optimization.

I think it's a successful remake, hopefully the remake of the first game will improve even more.

Silent Hill 2 is pure dark psychological horror done right.
It’s not about jump scares — it’s about guilt, trauma, and the kind of silence that feels heavier than noise. The atmosphere, sound design, and storytelling make everything feel deeply unsettling in the best way.

A haunting experience that stays with you long after you stop playing.

It's really a masterpiece in the survival horror genre. The story is interesting and well thought out. The characters are memorable, the puzzles satisfying and the gameplay enjoyable. Not to mention, the game is scary, at least to me it was. 

It's less of a visceral horror like that in the Resident Evil franchise and more of a psychological horror. The game drips with atmosphere and the soundtrack and sound design are excellent. I don't really have any complaints with it. I'd highly recommend if you enjoy survival horror and a unique, mysterious story to dive into.

As someone who has played all the old original Silent Hill games back in the day and seeing so many half arsed or butchered remakes I was sceptical at first about this but this game is absolute master class.

Sure it has changed a few things over the original but it's done it in a way that didn't feel disrespectful or to change it for the sake of it to put their own mark on it like other remakes seem to do with no regard for the original creation, where they simply use the games name as some sell out buzz word to guarantee sales.

However the Bloober team have yet again managed to capture the soul of the original game, created with love, attention to detail and paying homage to the history of the game.

From the gorgeous design, the expertly recreated atmosphere, the voice acting and character redesigns all faithfully coming together to make something truly beautiful. 

This is what I picture in my mind when I remember being a kid experiencing this game for the first time with my father - and now here I am as an adult playing it for myself, and to have a remake as masterfully done as this has been something very special for me.

claims.claim: Reviewers find the combat repetitive due to a limited variety of weapons and unchanging encounter mechanics.

citations.review_text:
This game has a great atmosphere and graphics are nice. It maintains its creepy atmosphere throughout the whole game, and the enemy designs are very well done. The story is also really good.

However, I find that the game drags on in some areas, like the hospital, which breaks immersion and leads to more frustrating moments rather than scary ones. The gameplay loop barely changes which can get tedious quickly. While the enemies are really interesting initially, they get old quick, besides some of the boss encounters. While you do eventually get a few weapon types, the combat remains the same; shoot an enemy to get them down and finish them with the melee weapon, so it gets old quickly. 

I am not even finished with the game but there are still 2 more areas for me to complete and it 's getting increasingly more tedious pushing through all the areas. 

The original defintely has better pacing and the time it takes to complete each area is a lot more reasonable. I will probably be taking a break from the game before I return to finish it because playing the game really does burn me out.

The combat ultimately brought this one down for me. Haven't completed a first playthrough, and I probably won't anytime soon. Combat is such a slog, and is so samey, and worst of all, largely no longer optional. If you see enemies you're expected to kill them. If you try to run away you realize most of them are as fast (if not faster) than you, and that they will follow you across half of the map to corner you if you try to run past. At least, in the open world. In the indoor sections you don't even get the choice to run. 

You get one melee weapon and three firearms, so combat feels exactly the same for the entire experience. This also means that the game's length works against it. You'd think that expanded areas and puzzles would be awesome, but not really the case here. It just means more backtracking and more insipid combat to slog through. I wanted to give this a shot, but to me SH2 Enhanced Edition is the infinitely superior way to experience this game. 

Bloober did a great job with everything surrounding the aesthetic and story, so I hope these awful gameplay decisions were forced in by Konami in an effort to pad the length of the game, because they make no sense for someone who actually wants to have fun while playing. I couldn't imagine having the patience to perform a second playthrough of this game. I couldn't even finish my first.

its a good remake sure, better than most remakes and remasters being released today, but its just too stretched out to the point its not even fun sometimes, just doing too much to make the game longer, original was 4-5 hours long while this is 11-12 hours long, combat can get repetitive so fast and the modern gameplay sure is more accessible but just makes the game way less unique and basic, feels like resident evil 2 remake, voice acting is also more basic and sounds like a netflix dub, its still a good game nonetheless, good for people who just cant stand tank controls because they're too hard and confusing!!!!! (honestly dude just grow up), i played original and remake back to back and i didn't grow up with ps2 games so this isn't nostalgia bias, oh and this game runs like poopoo too

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game does not hold the player's hand and features puzzles that can be uninformative or require backtracking.

citations.review_text:
Wow what a ride! This game is rare that it actually made scared to turn every corner and the story itself was tragic and enticing! 

Pros:
- Great Story
- Good Puzzles
- Insanely Good Level Design
- Good Voice Acting
- Godlike Sound Design

Cons:
- The performance is average at best (I have a good pc btw)
- The game doesn't hold your hand that much when it needs to

Great game! 
8/10

I have played numerous horror games over the years from outlast, resident evil, fnaf etc. I REALLY wanted to like this game i really did. BUT I think it is better as  love letter to the original fans who played it years ago as opposed to new people. The story is extremely slow, I understand that this is a mostly heavily symbolic game but that is just one of the issues. The enemies are very repetitive there is a monster with legs whose man goal is to run from you when you see it and just hide behind corners waiting to ambush you. The dread and atmosphere which they do a very good job at building is often wasted. The puzzles which were interesting and fun at first just became tedious and consistently slowed down the gameplay even more after the halfway point. Not to mention the constant back tracking through areas. So much so there is literally a section of the game where you spend hours in an area then get thrown into a type of "Upside down"(strangers thing reference) version of the exact same place you spent hours navigating. I was fortunate enough to not experience too many stuttering issues if I played at 1440p and locked the fps at 60. Though if you run through halls too fast the frames will drop. I respect this franchise as a classic and their fans. I also understand this game probably has some amazing lore that is better consumed in a video essay on YouTube than to play it. But after being ambushed by the same enemy(leg monster) hiding behind a wall for the 3rd time in 2 minutes EVEN WITH ME having maybe only 5 hours left in the game I just couldn't take it anymore and uninstalled it. 

My computer specs. Ryzen 7 3800x ,16Gb of DDR4, 5070ti

The game is fantastic! One of the best remakes to come to market. The story is phenomenal and really immersive, the plot as well as the encompassing combat elements really shine in this game. While, most of the puzzles are intuitive and easy to understand/solve - some of them can be quite "uninformative" and require taking a step back to get the bigger picture. All and all, the story really moved me and, there's not many games where I can say the story changed me as a person. Really Great stuff, the studio should be proud!

Overall, it's a good remake. I think it could have been a much more enjoyable experience if it lasted around 8 hours.

Cons:
- Having to clear buildings twice... clearing the original is OK, but the rusty versions are boring.
- The monsters respawning is BS.
- The open map is unnecessary. There's nothing important on the map, no reason is given to try to enter buildings, you can easily skip them, so why an open map? Also, not knowing where to go is frustrating. You're constantly running around in the streets with creatures everywhere.
- Good graphics but bad optimization.

I think it's a successful remake, hopefully the remake of the first game will improve even more.

citations.review_text: Horror classic that is a must play for anyone that is a fan of the genre or horror in general, my only complaint would be that the game is not optimized and sometimes can be very laggy depending on the section (so definitely get an optimization mod).

Like probably a lot of people, I was pretty skeptical when SH2 Remake got announced. I mean the OG is an all time classic and one of the best games of all time and Bloober is taking care of that? Oh boy.. 
The first trailer was horrible, James looked like crap and overall the whole atmosphere was weird.
Time went by, new trailers were released and they started to look way better. I would assume they were reacting to the feedback? Anyway, game released and I got curious after I watched some gameplay and decided to play it on PS5. (My old PC wasn't good enough.)
And damn, I was having a great time! 
The new actors are great, especially James, the soundtrack is still one of the best from any videogame (except "Unhinged Betrayal" - what were they thinking?) and the atmosphere is just unmatched. 
Graphics are also great and it did run well on highest settings except the Toluca prison. That was a mess with frame rates dropping down to 40 or 45 fps.
And yet I loved revisiting all these places that I still remembered so well. 
The remake is quite faithful to the original. Sure, they changed some of the ways you solve the riddles you already knew, or tweaked some dialogue, they even added some new elements but the outcome didn't change.

If you like horror games, go ahead and buy it. If you liked the original, go ahead and buy it. If you like videogames at all, just go ahead and buy it!
No seriously, I think it's one of the best remakes that we've gotten so far and I really can't wait for the Silent Hill 1 Remake. Please don't screw it up, Bloober!

PS.: it's a crime that this game doesn't have a photomode!

"In my restless dreams, I see that town." 

Silent Hill 2 is the best survival horror game I've ever played. Everything is well done: interesting puzzles, a good story and its presentation; you don't want to skip cutscenes because you're immersed in this strange yet captivating place. Throughout the game, you're constantly immersed in the unease; you feel it all along with James until the end of his journey. The only downside, for me, is OPTIMIZATION! Games have become increasingly demanding lately, and even on a good PC, it still managed to deliver low FPS at times, but if you overlook that, the game is definitely worth your attention. I'd love to see remakes of other games in this series.

Incredible remake of a classic Survival Horror game, perhaps made even better. The first game was a flawed masterpiece but this remake really brought out the best in the storyline and characters and to me, it excelled and became a better overall experience. I know some purists really love to hate on this remake but I will die on this hill - I think this is the best way to experience Silent Hill 2 and it's dark, at times depressing but wholly profound story and intense atmosphere.

No other horror game will top the intensity and foreboding that this game brings to the table. Toluca Prison will go down to me as the most aggressively oppressive video game level ever made, and this game does it justice. I both hated and loved experiencing some of these areas again, especially that place.

With just a bit over 20 hours, I played the game on Standard Difficulty with Standard puzzles, had a good time with some intense moments but I never died or came close to dying. Those looking for more of a challenge likely should play on Hard combat difficulty, although this game isn't about that. It's about the experience.

I liked the original Silent Hill 2 quite a bit from my memory but this remake made me love and appreciate the game so much more, that I think it might land in my top five games of all time.

The only gripes I had were Unreal Engine 5 performance hiccups, namely traversal and shader cache stuttering, otherwise I had a crash and the game, outside of those stutters, ran at a solid FPS with a mix of Medium/High settings on 1440p. Only recommend Ray tracing if you have a really beefy rig. 

With 8 endings (I received two) and new game +, this game has a fair amount of content and I recommend it to every fan of Survival Horror.

How they ♥♥♥♥ up what make Silent Hill, "Silent Hill". The original game was not this tension dialing to 10 all the time, original Silent Hill 2 has many respites, but this team make it impossible to feel the sadness and melancholy. Don't get me start with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ performance, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ trash optimization all over, as it always been for this studio, in all of their games, and they never learn or care to fix or to do better next time. This prove me right also with the latest game, Cronos: The New Dawn. I don't understand why everyone give them a pass with very positive reviews. Even though the graphic and atmosphere are amazing, but the unplayable stuttering is unforgivable, no matter the setting. I tried it on multiple machines and it's a stutter fest. I vow to never play any of their game again. I also don't understand why they give them the big IPs again and again, more so to let them ♥♥♥♥ it up. No matter the reviews scores or anyone says, no matter how well the sales, all of my experience with their games are horrendous. For SH2 Remake, I have to force myself to complete it and it took me 1 year and 7 months (582 days), why? because the stuttering make it unplayable and the dreadful and tension is too much to bear, someone might said I'm too weak but I completed Outlast 1 and 2 no problem. The thing is, the tension is very good if this is other game but too much like this doesn't feel like Silent Hill at all. I feel pressure, not longing, I feel disgust, not sadness, I feel I want to get away from it, not melancholy which make everyone love original SH. I don't have anything else to say about the game. Lastly maybe a bit personal, but who the ♥♥♥♥ think it's a good idea to name a studio "Bloober", as in like blooper, the mistake, the embarrassment, it also sound very unprofessional and doesn't encourage trust in anything you have your hands on.

Incredible remake. Outstanding work from the remake team!

I played the OG when I was a kid (I probably shouldn't have, I know 😂), and somehow this remake managed to bring back those same memories and feelings.

I really love how they stayed faithful to the original while making some slight changes to the combat, which, in my opinion, made the gameplay even better. The boss fights were also a big improvement over the original.

There are some small stutters here and there, probably due to UE5, but honestly, it's nothing major and it didn't really affect my experience.

Overall, an amazing remake and a great way to experience Silent Hill again.

Now I'm just waiting for the Silent Hill 1 remake...

**Take my money already! 😂**

This game has serious technical problems. Ghosting, stuttering, aliasing issues and poor optimization. It also starts pretty slowly and, for a while, feels almost boring.

But once it gets going, man, it gets going.

The atmosphere is absolutely insane. Environments feels suffocating and hostile, as if there's something deeply wrong at the most fundamental level. 

The graphics are grotesquely beautiful, the sound design is amazing, and the story becomes more disturbing the further you go.

And don't get me started on the boss fights. This game somehow concentrates many of the meanest, nastiest, and most brutal boss fights I have ever seen into one relatively short experience. 

Silent Hill 2 is sick.

It's by all means a fantastic remake narratively and does a pretty great job with adapting the gameplay and puzzles, but man we are approaching nearly 2 years since release and this game still unfourtantely has major stuttering and freezes that can make the experience really frustrating. I wouldn't say unplayable, but it's getting close.

Hats off to the sound design and environment, they are on point, perfect.

But I found myself really struggling when it comes to the game itself. While the audio and atmosphere are top-notch, the game is simply bloated and far too long. This is probably because it was stretched to 2–3 times the length of the original with the same content and that made the story pacing suffer.

The confusing maze-like level and puzzle design is clearly padded just to justify the high price tag. Having to open the map every single minute (well over 1,000 times in my case) was driving me insane. The inflated number of mannequins combined with its unsatisfying combat completely killed the horror element. At some point, I was no longer scared, just annoyed instead.

I haven't even mentioned the performance yet, which was also horrendous; constantly dropping to 35-40 FPS whether it was on the highest or lowest settings.

I've played both the original and this remake. The remake is worth your time and I found it even more enjoyable and scarier than the original. Team Bloober did an excellent job. That said, the game is marred by performance issues (stuttering and game crashes) irrespective of hardware. Were it not for that, I'd say this would be the definitive edition of the game.

Silent Hill 2, great game of all time!!

I spent 32 hours on it and loved every second. Even after getting all the endings, I still can’t stop thinking about it.

Visually, it’s one of the most stunning games I’ve ever played. The graphics, lighting, and environmental detail are simply top-tier, creating an atmosphere that feels hauntingly beautiful rather than merely terrifying. Walking through the forests and empty streets never got boring. Everything just feels mysterious and dreamlike. 

The game doesn’t rely on cheap jump scares. Instead, it slowly builds this constant feeling that something isn’t right. Even when nothing is happening, you’re still tense. That’s the kind of horror I love!

The soundtrack is fantastic too. Akira Yamaoka absolutely nailed it. Every piece of music fits perfectly, and even the sound effects stand out. The radio static is easily one of my favorite parts of the game. As soon as it starts crackling, your heart sinks. You know something is nearby, you can hear it, you can even feel it but can’t see it at first glance. It’s such a simple mechanic, but it’s incredibly effective.

The level design is excellent as well. The game keeps taking you somewhere new, so exploring never feels repetitive. You don’t have to stuck in the same place and waste time running around. I think the puzzles were really well designed. They’re challenging enough to make you think, but never so difficult that they become annoying.

The story is what really makes this game special. It’s creative, emotional, and full of moments that stay with you. It explores guilt, love, loss, and human nature in such a powerful way. Every big reveal hits hard, and the ending left me thinking about it long after the credits rolled.

Silent Hill 2 is absolutely a masterpiece. The atmosphere, music, story, and world all come together perfectly. I finished the game several days ago and still feel like I’m somewhere between reality and that fog-covered town. Without any doubt, this i…
Big fan of this remake with the combat, the map designs with the empty streets consumed by fog, the soundtrack, the characters, and the many endings. This game is a 10/10 must play.

Amazing game on its own legs, and a masterpiece of a remake on top of that. Thoroughly enjoyed my time with SH2R, even on subsequent playthroughs. The atmosphere, music, and visual design are what made the original stand out to me, and these aspects are back in full swing with this one too. Solid 10/10 for me, and hopefully for the majority of people who click with the game. Probably one of, if not the best example of how well and in-depth stories can be told through the video game medium.

You also get to stare at bread, I don't really know how you can improve from there, easy recommend.

Surprisingly, Bloober team really put their sweat and tears into this remake.

They've expanded the town, included additional sections, ensured they stayed very faithful to the PS2 game (with some minor changes like [spoiler]Eddie & Laura not being in Pete's Bowl-O-Rama but rather in a Movie Theatre to set a chase sequence with Laura in the Theatre[/spoiler]) and they even included 2 new endings. This is the most accessible and the best modern re-imagining of Silent Hill 2 you could get really. 

After completing the game and getting 2 of the classic endings [spoiler](In the water & Leave ending)[/spoiler], I've come to really appreciate the effort made altogether. With genuinely amazing performances by all the voice actors which amplifies the themes of trauma and emotional depth (Especially with James), terrifying music and sound design by the original composer Akira Yamaoka, and the art and monsters looking more terrifying than every by the original art director Masahiro Ito, buying this remake is a no brainer.

Obviously this doesn't replace the original, but if I were asked which version to recommend to someone wanting to get into Silent Hill, this remake is what I would recommend

I have been a big fan of the Silent Hill games for years, and this game's existence is a good sign that maybe we'll start to get more quality content again. The remake is actually quite a lot different from the original (both of which I have played), and it goes past simple graphics upgrades. The themes and story are still there in broad strokes, but a lot of the locations have been radically changed, and entire new story sections have been added. The gameplay and movement is more dynamic, which makes sense if youre trying to appeal to wider, more modern audiences.

It takes about twice as long to finish the remake than it does the original game. I do have some minor gripes with the more action-oriented gameplay, but overall it is a very solid game and honestly shouldnt simply be compared to its source material, because it stands very well on its own. To be fair, some parts of this game are definitely much scarier than the original, and the general vibe/atmosphere is mostly intact.

Original Silent Hill 2 is one of my favorite games of all time, if not straight up the favorite. That said, the remake is better than I could possibly hope for, considering Bloober’s previous, less-than-stellar attempts at psychological horror and Konami in general. But yeah, it’s competent and perhaps the fourth or fifth best Silent Hill game. It plays and looks well; this is the first time western developers have managed to successfully emulate that feverish atmosphere, and most importantly, they mostly managed not to butcher the story too badly.

Did they manage to do as good as the original Silent Hill 2? In short: hеll no.

Some of it is absolutely the baby-duck syndrome, when people like me who’ve played the original game dozens of times automatically like the new take less, just because. For example, I hate all the new winks to that one specific theory with burning passion, but I understand that it’s mostly just me.

But I swear, this is far from the remake’s only problem.

First, this game is stretched so thin that the pacing is dead. You have to spend about 15-20 hours playing this thing; the original was about 6. And there is not nearly enough meat to justify that length. There are about three new cutscenes, some walkie-talkie bits, and one new enemy variant. The rest is basically the same as the original but with a boatload more backtracking and fighting the same four enemies. Now every area in this game seems to require a hub puzzle with many connected puzzles, and believe me it gets old fast. The Silent Hill Historical Society stretch is straight up wrecked because of this. In the original it was a poster child for pacing in horror, with something mad happening every ten minutes or so. Not now - prepare to meander around the prison for an hour minimum and then spend an eternity backtracking through labyrinth.

Second, it just doesn’t hit the same, and I think, aside from pacing, it’s because of the voice acting and the music - the latter being the most …

I've always been a big Silent Hill fan, and let me tell you, this remake cooked. Combat has been improved immensely, going from enemies being a minor nuisance in the original to actually having to deal with them as a threat now. The story on the other hand still holds up in my opinion. I can't say too much without spoiling, but it is truly a testament to psychological horror. Also, parts of the story have gotten vastly updated, so much so that small sections in the original are now far, bigger ones. And let me tell you, those sections actually gave me some downright dread that I haven't experienced since Silent Hill 4. If I had to pick one gripe, it'd have to be some of the motion capture. You can tell right away that when they have to do exaggerated expressions that it just doesn't work too well. But other than that, it's still pretty good I'd say. Way better than some of the hammy acting in the original, which was charming in its own way. But yeah, if you're a big horror/Silent Hill fan, highly recommend.

The greatest survival horror game of all time with a fresh new coat of paint. Although some portions have been remixed or removed, the remake adds a lot more content. The typical playthrough will take around 12-16 hours, which is much longer than the original. The voice acting is great, and who could forget the brilliant soundtrack by the one and only Akira Yamaoka. This is by far one of my favorite games of all time.

"In my restless dreams, I see that town. Silent Hill."

Having the played the original way back when I was 14 years old on my friend's ps2, playing the remake of the beloved 2001 classic felt like remembering a long lost core memory that was hidden in the depths of my mind. However this time, having gotten older and more mature, I am able to appreciate the themes, characters and story of this game at a greater level.

Setting: You play as James Suntherland, a guy mourning the death of his wife but mysteriously get a letter from his late wife that tells him to visit the foggy town of silent hill. The game does a excellent job setting a moody and depressing atmosphere right from the beginning through the use of fog, rain and dreary colours in the town's various run down and abandoned buildings that give off a serene but also opressive feel to each location. The various places of silent hill that James explores almost feels like a character in itself, starting off as derelict areas that are silent and dreamlike but later on shift and morph into surreal shapes and nightmarish, reality-defying architecture that reflect James's disturbed state of mind. Compared to the OG, areas in the remake are much larger and expansive, with lots of hidden areas to explore.

Gameplay: The tank controls and the fixed camera angle from the OG are gone in favour of a 3rd person view with more modernised controls as James moves more nimble now. The various iconic enemies from the OG also look and behave just like how I rembered them, with updated graphics that brings to life all their disturbing and symbolic designs. Combat is a HUGE improvement from the OG since James can now dodge attacks and aim more precise. Boss fights are more interesting with a certain one being a huge upgrade from the OG. The selection of weapons are the exact same as the OG, including melee weapons like the plank of wood and trusty steel pipe and ranged weapons include the pistol, shotgun and hunting rifle. Combat …

As someone with extensive expertise in horror and shooter games, and a deep devotion to the Silent Hill series, I went into Silent Hill 2 Remake with extremely high expectations. My first playthrough took around 25 hours on the hardest difficulty, and I can confidently say Bloober Team delivered one of the most respectful remakes I've ever played.

What makes it work is that it never loses sight of what made the original Silent Hill 2 so exceptional. The expanded environments, modernized combat, and incredible visual presentation add to the experience without compromising the original's identity, atmosphere, or psychological horror. It feels less like a replacement and more like a genuine continuation of the original's vision.

Eddie Dombrowski is where the writing reaches another level. His association with the "Gluttonous Pig" is far more than a joke about his weight. The tablet in Toluca Prison explicitly represents Eddie, tying him to the sin of gluttony, while his constant eating—pizza in the bowling alley and food during the remake—becomes part of his characterization.

But the brilliance is in what that symbolism actually represents. Eddie's "gluttony" isn't simply about food; it's about consumption, resentment, humiliation, and ultimately violence. He has spent his entire life consuming the hatred other people have directed toward him until it becomes part of his identity. His tragedy is that he eventually turns that pain outward, consuming others through violence in the same way he believes the world consumed and dehumanized him. His Otherworld—a freezing meat locker filled with grotesque bodies of meat—literally turns his self-image into his environment.

That makes Eddie such an incredible foil to James. Both men are killers, both are psychologically broken, and both are drawn to Silent Hill—but James desperately tries to preserve his denial, while Eddie completely surrenders to his. Eddie's final descent isn't just a boss fight; it's the culminat…

Silent Hill 2 Remake doesn’t even feel like a remake. It feels more like a continuation of the original story, a return to Silent Hill, where James comes back once again and we experience his story from a fresh perspective.

The atmosphere is absolutely phenomenal. The fog, sound design, lighting, and disturbing environments create a constant feeling of unease. The story remains one of the strongest aspects, and the remake expands the characters and world without losing the psychological depth of the original.

The combat is smoother and more satisfying, but it still feels like survival horror rather than an action game. Most importantly, it respects the original instead of trying to replace it.

Beautiful, disturbing, emotional, and genuinely unsettling. It feels less like someone remade Silent Hill 2 and more like we were given another chance to walk through James’s nightmare.

Silent Hill 2 Remake is a masterclass in respectful reinvention. Few games carry the weight of Silent Hill 2. It's not just a horror game; it's one of gaming's most profound psychological journeys. And the remake manages to honor that weight. The level desi- every hallway, apartment, and hospital corridor feels intentional, like the town itself is a character. The fog isn't just ambiance; it's a mechanic. It shapes the dread, limits your sight, and amplifies the unknown. And the enemies, so thoughtfully placed, make each encounter feel meaningful instead of routine. The graphics, gorgeous. The sound design, genuinely unnerving, in the best way. And importantly, it keeps the heart of the original. James' emotional journey still lands just as hard, maybe harder now, with the modern visuals serving the story. This is how remakes should be done. It's not a replacement, it's a second cornerstone. 10 out of 10 for me. A gold standard for horror remakes

A fantastic return to a classic. The story is still emotional, disturbing, and faithful to the original, with a few modern touches that hit hard. The gameplay feels smoother and more responsive while keeping that slow, tense survival‑horror style. Graphics are a huge upgrade  detailed environments, creepy creature designs, and amazing lighting that boosts the atmosphere. Performance is solid, and the whole game feels darker, heavier, and more immersive. A strong remake that respects the original while modernising everything that matters.

I played the game when it came out and the technical issues(hitching, frame drops, ghosting) were so awful and haven't gone back since I finished it. I wonder if it got better.

I never got very far into the original and I'm so glad this remake exists. This allowed me experience such an amazing story that I almost overlooked. [i]Silent peak :)[/i]
Shout-out to polish bloober team, because sh2 is best horror game I recently played. Great story and even better atmosphere, all locations are very veryyy creepy and mysterious, and special effects and music + scary sounds (whispers, cries etc.) made me feel on edge and stressed the whole game. Only minus imo is that after playing for awhile fighting enemies become monotonous and feels like a chore :/.
But overall I think it's worth the price and worth playing at least once :).

This is a largely faithful adaptation to the original material, in terms of story tone and character behavior as well as the lore documents you find. The combat can be a bit of a slog but that's never really been the strong point of this franchise. Admittedly, certain sections of the game seem to drag on for longer than necessary, but that is a minor flaw in an otherwise excellent re-imagining of a cornerstone of videogame horror media. It is absolutely worth your time if you have any love for the series. Congratulations to bloober team for knocking this (almost) entirely out of the park.
